question_text: Find the rank of the matrix with rows (1, 2, 1), (−1, 0, 2) and (0, 1, −1).

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the rank of this matrix.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Test the 3×3 determinant
steps.margin_note: First mark. The matrix is 3×3, so the rank is at most 3. Expand the whole determinant and see whether it is zero.
steps.memory_tip: Start at the largest minor — for a 3×3 matrix that is the whole determinant.

recall.must_convey: That the full 3×3 determinant is expanded first and comes to −5.
accept: expand the whole three by three determinant first
the determinant works out to minus five
take the largest minor which is the full determinant
full determinant expand cheste minus five vasthundi
one into zero minus two, minus two into one, plus one into minus one

steps.why: Rank is the order of the largest non-zero minor, so the search starts at the top order and works down only if that one is zero.
common_mistakes: Dropping a minus sign inside a 2×2 minor, such as writing (−1)(−1) = −1.
Reading a rank off the original matrix with no test at all.

steps.label: State the rank
steps.margin_note: Second mark. A non-zero minor of order 3 exists, and a 3×3 matrix has no minor of order 4, so 3 is the largest order possible.
steps.memory_tip: A non-zero 3×3 determinant settles it at once — the rank is the full 3.

steps.why: One non-zero minor of order 3 is enough, and no minor of order 4 exists to rule out, so the answer is complete.
common_mistakes: Going on to test 2×2 minors when the 3×3 one is already non-zero.
Writing the value −5 as the rank.
